content_of_post_to_comment:
I have the same goals as most of the people here, to reduce phone usage, get good sleep, not procrastinate, get out of porn (especially) i.e. to get disciplined. My life has been running on a loop, trying to get away from all my distractions. I get extremely motivated to quit all that is distracting, do so successfully for a few days or weeks, then fail at it. I go into the the phase of sadness and demotivation for a few days, all my bad habits aggravate during that period. I get back from it, only to fall in the same cycle again. This has started to become really tiring. I don't how much more I can sustain all this pressure. All the overly hyping short-content, brainrot and porn has completely changed the way I think (I am not kidding).

This may not be the right subreddit, but I have nearly reached the conclusion that I can't quit porn. I am heavily addicted to it. I have put so much effort, as far as to create my own computer application to block porn. But, nothing worked in the long term. Porn has become a coping mechanism.

I believe the only solution to this is a complete mindset shift or personality change, address the issues underneath. How should I achieve this? How can I change the way that I think? What would be a good first step? I am open to book suggestions, videos, anything, but preferably based on scientific methods, something that is realistic and sustainable. I don't want that overly motivating, grindset kind of thing. Completely unrelated, but would posting to some other subreddits help? Thanks in advance.
comment: Building a blocker and still ending up back at porn says a lot about why another round of willpower probably won’t fix this. If it’s become a coping mechanism, I’d experiment with catching the moment before the urge: what happened, what feeling you’re trying to escape, and what you actually need. Changing that loop seems more sustainable than trying to become a completely different person.
